subject: Multi-entity remittance mapping & cash-apply workflow for HealthBridge Q4 invoices
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthbridge.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0500
Subject: Invoice split: HealthBridge Q4 remittance questions

Hi Irene / Marissa,

We're finalizing our AP run for Q4 and want to confirm how Redwood wants remittances routed when invoices are split across Redwood entities. Our system (WorkPay) can send a single ACH/virtual card payment, but we need clear rules for: 1) which legal entity should receive funds for each invoice line, 2) VAT handling per entity, and 3) how to include cost center tags so our cash application team posts to the right P&L.

Can you share a compact spec or a sample CSV we can send with the payment? Also, we saw different remit addresses on prior invoices — we want to avoid short-pays or mis-applied credits.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Finance Operations
HealthBridge

Attachments referenced: HB-Q4-invoice-split-spec.xlsx (requested)
From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthbridge.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Invoice split: HealthBridge Q4 remittance questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear questions.

Summary answer up-front: we support a single payment from your AP (ACH or virtual card) with a remittance CSV that maps each invoice line to a Redwood legal entity and cost center. Our cash-apply service will auto-split and route funds to the correct internal ledgers; for cross-entity VAT we require the VAT ID per line so we can book tax liability in the right jurisdiction.

I've attached a sample CSV (remit-mapping-sample.csv) and a short PDF with ledger mapping conventions (redwood-ledger-mapping-notes.pdf). Key fields in the CSV: invoice_number, invoice_line_id, amount, remit_entity (Redwood US | Redwood EMEA), remit_account (bank account identifier), vat_rate, vat_id, cost_center_code, PO_number.

Notes / constraints:
- For multi-entity invoices we prefer the payment to be single-origin with the CSV attached; if you send multiple separate payments we will apply them but it increases reconciliation time and may delay credits.
- Refunds/credits are issued to the same remit_entity that was credited at the time of invoice issuance.
- If VAT is charged by a Redwood EMEA entity, include the VAT ID to ensure correct VAT reporting; missing VAT IDs will cause us to hold the line pending manual review.

Could you confirm your AP can attach the CSV to the payment instruction? If yes, we'll provide a one-page implementation checklist for your payments vendor.

Thanks — I'll loop in Karthik for the ledger mapping specifics.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Finance Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachments: remap sample (remit-mapping-sample.csv), ledger notes (redwood-ledger-mapping-notes.pdf)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthbridge.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Invoice split: Invoice_line -> ledger mapping and cost center policy

Elena — quick technical follow-up from ledger side.

Two implementation patterns we support:
1) Per-line remit_entity: each invoice line contains remit_entity + remit_account. Your single payment aggregates total amount; our cash-apply engine splits by remit_account and posts to the entities accordingly. This is preferred when different business units own distinct lines.
2) Primary-entity plus reallocation: payment goes to a primary Redwood entity; we then internally reclassify revenue via intercompany entries to the final entity. Use this only when your AP cannot support per-line remittance fields.

For VAT handling, include the VAT_ID field exactly as recorded on the invoice (case-sensitive). For cost centers, we will accept either your internal cost_center_code or our mapped cost center (we can provide a mapping table). Example CSV row: 

"INV-2026-409,1,540.00,Redwood EMEA,EMEA-ACC-03,20%,GB123456789,ENG-PLATFORM,PO-99871"

I've attached a one-page mapping (HB-Q4-invoice-split-spec.xlsx) with sample rows; Marissa can coordinate a short handoff call with your AP vendor if needed.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Revenue Operations

Thanks Karthik / Irene — that helps. A couple of clarifying items from our AP team (copied):

1) Our payment system can attach one CSV per ACH batch. We'll include invoice_number and invoice_line_id. Can you confirm the maximum number of lines you can accept before we need to chunk the file?
2) For refunds: if the original payment was to the primary entity and then reallocated, who do we make the refund out to? Primary entity or final owner?
3) Are there any particular SWIFT/BIC bank note fields we should populate when sending cross-border USD->GBP to ensure GBP lines land to Redwood EMEA account?

Payments team will run a test batch next Tuesday.

Elena

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthbridge.com>, payments@healthbridge.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Invoice split: Invoice_line -> ledger mapping and cost center policy

Hi Elena / Payments team — quick answers below and a proposed test plan: 

1) File size / line limit: our cash-apply pipeline comfortably handles up to 25,000 line entries per batch. For AP systems that chunk by invoice, we recommend groups no larger than 5,000 lines to keep batch processing predictable.

2) Refund policy: refunds should be routed to the remit_entity that received the original payment. If you remit to a primary entity and we performed internal reallocation, we'll still expect refunds to go to the original remit_account. We can annotate the refund with the final-owner entity in the refund memo to aid your reconciliation.

3) Bank note fields for cross-border: include the beneficiary BIC and the explicit remit_account identifier we provide in the CSV; for USD->GBP instruct your bank to use 'Beneficiary account' (do not use intermediary narrative fields). We'll provide the exact BIC/account lines in the implementation checklist.

Proposed test plan (next Tue):
- You send a small ACH batch (3 invoices, 6 lines) with remit CSV attached to payments@healthbridge.com and cc irene.
- Our cash-apply team will process and send a short report showing ledger entries, VAT bookings, and cost center attribution.

I'll coordinate the checklist and sample BICs. Vivek — can you confirm we can expose the mapping table for HealthBridge's cost center codes (one-time share, SSO link)?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Billing & Collections
Redwood Inference

Elena / Payments team — confirmed. I'll share a secure Drive folder with a cost-center mapping CSV and the one-page checklist (link above). Access will be granted to the emails on this thread. A few implementation tips from accounting: 

- Ensure your CSV uses UTF-8 and commas (no embedded line breaks in fields).
- If you include PO_number, we can auto-attach PO references to revenue lines which speeds matching.
- For mixed-currency invoices, include both invoice_currency and remit_currency columns; we will perform FX at the time of receipt using the payout entity's daily rate.

We'll expect your test batch on Tuesday morning; Marissa will coordinate the post-test validation. If the test passes, we'll publish the checklist and you can move to full-volume processing.
